findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a concrete proving command (e.g. `python -c "import ast, sys; src=open('src/.../transport.py').read(); tree=ast.parse(src); names={n.name for n in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(n, (ast.FunctionDef,ast.ClassDef))}; assert not names & {'_with_connection_retry','TlsVerificationError','_tls_verification_error','_as_backend_http_error','_connection_retry_exceptions','_jira_http_error_types'}, names"` or an equivalent `grep -cE` to AC1 so that 'transport.py no longer defines them' is machine-verifiable.
evidence: The Testing section states 'the oracle for a pure relocation is that the EXISTING suite passes unedited', which is silent on deletion of originals
A test importing TlsVerificationError from transport passes whether transport defines it natively or re-exports it from retry.py
No grep / AST / wc -l check is specified to assert the six defs are absent from transport.py post-move
findings.finding: AC1 asserts 'transport.py no longer defines them' but provides no proving command to verify the originals were deleted rather than left in place alongside the re-exports. The existing test suite would pass either way (it only exercises behaviour, not source location), so the 'no longer defines' sub-claim is unverified.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria — AC1: 'retry.py exists and contains all six named members, and transport.py no longer defines them'
scenarios: An executor moves the cluster to retry.py, adds re-exports, but forgets to delete the originals — tests stay green, the circular-import check passes, yet AC1's 'no longer defines' clause is silently false
The module-size gate also fails silently because the originals were never removed, yet no AC cross-checks this specifically
findings.suggested_fix: Append to AC1: 'verified by `grep -En "^(def|class) (_with_connection_retry|TlsVerificationError|_tls_verification_error|_as_backend_http_error|_connection_retry_exceptions|_jira_http_error_types)" src/.../transport.py` returning no matches.'

findings.finding: AC5 requires transport.py to be 'under the 800-line cap with headroom for S2', but S2's size (number of lines it will add) is not stated anywhere in this plan, so 'headroom for S2' is an unquantified threshold that an executor cannot deterministically pass or fail.

scenarios: If S2 adds 30 lines and this story only frees 20, the headroom criterion is technically unsatisfied, but the executor has no way to know this from the plan
